summary: Frontend-only test of Customer app 'Video Stories' feature at mobile 430x900. Home renders, an 'AzoApp Stories' row appears below Categories with exactly 3 story cards (app-story-card-0/1/2) titled 'Deep Home Cleaning', 'Salon at Home', 'AC Service'. Tapping card 0 opens the full-screen viewer (testID story-viewer) which contains progress segments, avatar+title header, story-mute (toggles VolumeX/Volume2), story-close, tap zones story-prev/story-next (verified navigation forward + backward), and CTA 'Book Cleaning' (story-cta) which closes viewer and navigates to /services. onEnded wiring for auto-advance IS correct — dispatching an 'ended' event programmatically advanced 'Deep Home Cleaning' -> 'Salon at Home'. HOWEVER natural auto-advance is BROKEN in practice because the seeded sample video URL (https://commondatastorage.googleapis.com/gtv-videos-bucket/sample/ForBiggerBlazes.mp4) returns HTTP 403 from this environment, giving the <video> element error code 4 (MEDIA_ELEMENT_ERROR: Format error), networkState=3 (NO_SOURCE), readyState=0, duration=NaN. Video never plays, so the browser never fires 'ended' and users see only the poster.

ui_bugs.issue: Sample video URL https://commondatastorage.googleapis.com/gtv-videos-bucket/sample/ForBiggerBlazes.mp4 returns 403 from the preview sandbox, so the <video> fails to load (error code 4, MEDIA_ELEMENT_ERROR: Format error). As a result the video never plays, only the poster shows, and natural AUTO-ADVANCE (which is driven by the video 'ended' event) never fires. Manual dispatch of 'ended' does advance to the next story, confirming the code wiring is correct — this is a video source/availability issue.

action_items: Replace the seeded sample video URL with a source that is reachable from the preview environment. Candidates: https://www.w3schools.com/html/mov_bbb.mp4, https://test-videos.co.uk/vids/bigbuckbunny/mp4/h264/360/Big_Buck_Bunny_360_10s_1MB.mp4, or self-host in the app's public assets. Verify via `curl -I <url>` from the container returns 200 and Content-Type video/mp4.

Optional: in StoryVideo.web.tsx, add an onError handler that (a) logs, and (b) calls onEnded after a fallback timeout so a broken/unplayable video still auto-advances instead of freezing on the poster.
critical_code_review_comments: Stories.tsx StoryViewer progress bar is static: current segment is hard-coded to width '60%' (line 71) instead of tracking video.currentTime/duration. Not a blocker for the requested acceptance tests but functionally the progress indicator does not reflect playback progress.
StoryVideo.web.tsx has no onError handler; a broken video silently stalls the story (poster only) and blocks auto-advance. Consider a fallback timer or onError -> onEnded().

success_rate.frontend: 88% (7/8 checks pass; only natural auto-advance via video 'ended' fails due to unreachable seeded video URL)

context_for_next_testing_agent: All UI testIDs are in place and behave correctly: app-story-card-0..2, story-viewer, story-video, story-mute, story-close, story-prev, story-next, story-cta. Only remaining fix is the sample video source URL — after main agent swaps it, re-open first story on mobile 430x900, do NOT toggle mute (autoplay only works while muted), wait for the video to actually start (v.paused===false, v.duration>0), then verify title changes from 'Deep Home Cleaning' -> 'Salon at Home' after the clip ends (or seek to duration-0.3 to force it).
rca of the issue: Root cause of auto-advance failure: the seeded story video URL (commondatastorage.googleapis.com/gtv-videos-bucket/sample/ForBiggerBlazes.mp4) responds with HTTP 403 from the preview container. The HTMLVideoElement therefore transitions to networkState=NO_SOURCE / error code 4 (Format error) and never emits the 'ended' event. Since StoriesViewer's auto-advance is driven exclusively by <video onEnded={next}>, playback ending is impossible when playback never starts. Fix: use a reachable MP4 URL (verified 200 via HEAD from the container) or add an onError fallback in StoryVideo.web.tsx that invokes onEnded after N seconds so the viewer degrades gracefully.
